title: How the active break-glass grant and its incident reach rwb-document on a document content read is not stated
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-039 section 4 step 7 and section 7 AC2 (every entry written for the user until 14:30 carries the grant ID and the incident); RWB-P4-E1039-CON 12.2 and 12.8 (the session answer and its break-glass state); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-11 and DP-19
section: s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow; s7 Acceptance criteria (AC3); s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story marks every entry written while a grant is active with the grant ID and the incident reference, and after the split the grant is rwb-access's and the entry is written by the reading service. The access contract publishes GET /me/session with the break-glass state and the end time, but no source states how rwb-document obtains the grant ID and the incident reference on a content read: whether they travel as a signed, short-lived claim in the session envelope that gateway-bff forwards, or whether the service calls the session read once per request, and how long a cached answer may be reused. Without that decision AC3 cannot be built or tested, and the fail-closed rule cannot say what happens when the session answer does not arrive.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-039 section 4 step 7: 'marks every entry written while the grant is active with the grant ID and the incident reference'; RWB-P4-E1039-CON 12.2: 'GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session ... the break-glass state with the end time the document declares for the banner'; no source says how a consuming service receives the grant on its own requests.
proposed: Fix in RWB-P4-E1039-CON how the grant ID and the incident reference are carried to a consuming service (claim or call), their lifetime and the reuse bound, and add the mechanism to the session contract; until then the service takes a signed claim from the forwarded session envelope and treats a missing or expired claim as no grant.

title: The capability-area code, the result code and the field list of a document content read in an access entry are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-039 sections 7 AC9 and 11 (area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, right R; DF-DEC-014 actions carry area, right, fields, filter, row count, grant and incident); Technical Specification P5 v2 T6.1 and API-P5-004 ('Documents, right R, scope applied'); RWB-P4-E1039-CON 11 (the entry shape)
section: s7 Acceptance criteria (AC1); s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s13 Solution plan
description: An access entry states a capability area, a right and a result, and for a case read it also lists the field IDs returned with their masking position. For a document content read the API declares the capability as Documents with right R, but no source gives the exact area code string an entry carries (DOCUMENTS, DOCUMENT or the document hub module code), the result value of a served read, or whether a content read (which returns a binary body and no field values) lists any field ID at all. AC1 and AC6 of this story need those three answers to state a record the central ledger and the access log can group and filter on.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-039 AC9: 'area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, right R and no case ID'; AC1: 'its actions list the field IDs returned, with DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked masked'; TSD P5 v2 API-P5-004: 'Authorization Documents, right R, scope applied' and 'Response Binary'; RWB-P4-E1039-CON 11 gives capabilityArea and result without a code list.
proposed: Add the capability-area code list that includes the document hub, the result code list and the rule for a read with no field values to the reference data or to RWB-P4-E1039-CON; until then the area is DOCUMENTS, the result is the legacy success value and a content read lists no field ID.

title: Which reads of the document hub other than the content read write an access entry in the target is not fixed
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-039 section 1 and AC4 (a document read is logged); Technical Specification P5 v2 API-P5-004, API-P5-009 ('each search written to the access log') and API-P5-011 ('each read written to the access log'); FSD P5 A2.6 and the DOCUMENT_SEARCH event of legacy RWB-E1-033
section: s1 Story; s7 Acceptance criteria (AC1, AC5); s16 Test cases; s19 Out of scope
description: The legacy key logs the read of a document and the modules log a search and an intake read in their own stories, and the technical specification repeats 'each search written to the access log' and 'each read written to the access log' for API-P5-009 and API-P5-011. No source states which of the P5 reads is served by this key's recorder after the split: the metadata read of API-P5-003 returns extracted personal fields and is arguably the read most in need of an entry, the search of API-P5-009 carries its own DOCUMENT_SEARCH event of legacy RWB-E1-033, and the intake reads belong to the intake key. This story keeps the content read only and the other stories reuse the recorder, which is a ruling the sources do not state.
evidence: TSD P5 v2 API-P5-009 purpose: 'each search written to the access log'; API-P5-011 purpose: 'each read written to the access log'; FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-006-01: 'one access event DOCUMENT_SEARCH ... RWB-E1-033'; legacy RWB-E1-039 AC4 names only GET /documents/{documentId}/content.
proposed: Rule in the P5 contract which reads write an entry and under which decision code, and state the owner of each entry; until then only the content read is owned here and the metadata, search and intake reads keep their own legacy keys and wire the same recorder.

title: The incident queue name and the session-answer reuse bound of the content read are not specified
source: Legacy story RWB-E1-039 section 5 X1 ('an incident is raised') and section 7 AC7 ('the platform administrator queue'); Template and Rules R5.5 DP-06 and R5.5 default ruling on parameters (P3 rwb-case)
section: s13 Solution plan (Configuration); s5 Exception paths (X1, X8); s12.8 Contract fakes
description: The legacy story raises an incident to the platform administrator queue when the access entry cannot be written, and this story repeats that path when the record fails. No source names that queue in the target, gives the reuse bound of the cached session answer that carries the grant, or states whether the raise goes through the parameters-driven incident route of the platform. Two configuration values therefore have no source, and the exception path of AC2 and X8 depends on both.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-039 X1: 'the read or export returns no data; status 503; an incident is raised'; AC7: 'the system raises an incident to the platform administrator queue'; no queue name, reuse bound or parameter key appears in TSD P5 v2 or in RWB-P4-E1039-CON.
proposed: Name the incident queue and the reuse bound in the platform observability and parameters baseline, and record them as parameter rows; until then the queue is a parameter of this service and the session answer is reused within one request only.
